summary:
BOOK 1 NOTES: "Elsie's Widowhood" (Martha Finley, Gutenberg 38353; 25 chapters)

Preface: Written for Elsie's fans; the public demanded a widowhood book. Theme: Christ's love makes life happy under bereavement. Quote: "I am filled with comfort, I am exceeding joyful in all our tribulation."

Epigraph: Holmes, "Alone she wanders where with HIM she trod... she leans on God."

CH I: Vi (Violet, ~daughter, youngest-age-sister of Elsie) finds mother Elsie (Mrs. Travilla) weeping with Elsie's face in mother's lap. Mother says "We cannot keep her always; some one wants to take her." Lester Leland (sculptor, poor artist, going to Italy in a few weeks, 1-3 yrs) engaged to Elsie. Father Edward Travilla (Mr. Travilla) jokes; grandpa Dinsmore (Horace Dinsmore, Elsie's father) mentioned. Mr. Travilla: "grace groweth best in winter." Elsie lays head on husband's breast; she fears leaning on him too much. Vi tells Elsie "I wish Lester Leland had never seen her." Elsie is happy; Vi says "I'm sure there's not another man... like papa." Vi tells Molly (Molly Percival, crippled cousin, writer/translator, mother Enna Johnson, brother Dick) of engagement. Molly envies; resolves to trust Christ. Molly's mother Enna was once proud, now docile/feeble-minded.

CH II: Lester sails to Italy. Engagement announced by note with invitation to family dinner at Ion. Reactions: Oaks (Horace Dinsmore Sr. and Jr. and wives; Bob & Betty Johnson), Ashlands (Carringtons; Herbert "as it isn't Vi"), Pinegrove (Howards), Fairview (Lester's family), Roselands (Mrs. Louise Conly, grandfather Mr. Dinsmore, sons Calhoun, Arthur, Isadore/Isa, daughter Virginia; Walter). Mrs. Conly calls it a mesalliance. Calhoun defends Leland. Virginia calls Lester "goody-goody." Rose Lacey (Mrs. Rose Dinsmore's sister; Laurels) and son. Lester departs after a few happy weeks; Elsie mourns.

CH III: September. Elsie and children on lakelet boat. Mr. Travilla stricken with sudden illness (agonizing abdominal pain). Dr. Arthur Conly, Dr. Barton called; city consult. Aunt Chloe (old nurse). Elsie nursing. Doctors' verdict: fatal. Mr. Travilla gives children blessings; tells Elsie "Precious little wife." Dinsmore tells him he will be father to children. Travilla: "I go to the glory." Chloe: "He's mos' dar."

CH IV: Travilla dies. Little daughter Lily (dead, buried beside). Last words to Edward ("My son... take your father's place"), Harold, Herbert, Walter (age 4), Molly, Enna. Burial beside Lily. Elsie collapses; Dinsmore takes her to Ion-area rooms. Elsie: "My seven darlings" (children named: Edward, Elsie (namesake, eldest daughter), Violet "Vi", Harold, Herbert, Walter, Rosie (Rose)). Mr. Dinsmore comforts her with Isaiah 43.

CH V: Children's grief; Rose comforts; Elsie prays with Vi. Little Rosie: Jesus "the way." Mammy/nurse. Elsie's room. Molly and Enna at supper; Enna scolds Molly; Molly weeps. Elsie allowed to see mother who remains in room.

CH VI: Life at Ion. Mr. Dinsmore moves to Ion. Edward to college (Edward away; Lester Leland still abroad). Estate left to Elsie for life, then Edward. Dinsmore, Elsie joint executors/guardians. Dinsmore teaches Harold & Herbert. Edward's talk with mother re: skepticism, college. Liberal allowance.

CH VII: November. Arthur Conly suggests Viamede (Florida/Louisiana Teche country plantation) for winter for grandfather's health. Elsie agrees. Molly and Enna invited. Isa invited too. Mrs. Conly and Virginia scorn it. Rosie & Walter; Walter "I wish my dear papa tum back." Calhoun Conly: grandfather's favorite.

CH VIII: New Orleans. Mr. Horace Dinsmore meets beggar George Boyd (Mrs. Carrington's nephew, previous would-be murderer of Travilla; maimed right hand; scarred by "Aunt Dicey's scalding shower"). Dinsmore feeds him. Elsie decides Boyd moved to Viamede wing; aunt Mrs. Carrington invited.

CH IX: Mrs. Carrington arrives. Boyd bedridden. Viamede: Mrs. Travilla's charitable works. Vi's/Harold's scoldings; Elsie makes the Latin lesson lesson (Herbert and Harold). Elsie teaches about work and talents. Herbert "lack of perseverance."

CH X: Elsie's church at Viamede; minister Mr. Jones (heterodox, claims one devil). Bible study with children; discussion on Satan, demons, angels, chains and darkness. Mr. Dinsmore, Cruden's Concordance. Mrs. Travilla: "keep close to Christ."

CH XI: Boyd dies in despair ("Too late... the door is shut"); last words "God be merciful to me a sinner." Mrs. Carrington distraught. Mrs. Travilla explains death to children.

CH XII: Miriam Pettit's girls' prayer meeting at Mason's former cottage; Vi and Elsie agree to lead prayer. Mr. Embury (Magnolia Hall owner, widower, wife Mary dead two years, two boys at school, two little girls) visits. Uncle Ben: Jones should not be retained. Mr. Embury and Mrs. Travilla's conversation; Mr. Jones dismissed by Mr. Embury's judgment.

CH XIII: Mr. Keith (Cyril Keith, grandson of Dinsmore cousin Marcia Keith, Pleasant Plains, Indiana) preaches ("They hated me without a cause"). Stays at Viamede. Friendly with Isa (Isadore Conly); Molly loves Mr. Embury's attentions; Embury and Keith rivals.

CH XIV: Molly rebellious, weeps for lost love, decides Christ alone. Mr. Embury's attention; Molly believes she is loved. Elsie warns.

CH XV: Dinsmore & Elsie discuss; Embury proposes to Molly in garden (children Corinna and Madie, sons Louis and Fred). Cyril & Isa courtship.

CH XVI: Embury & Molly engaged; Magnolia Hall (house, Embury's). Dick (Molly's brother, doctor) arrives. Molly & Embury wedding; Keith officiates; bridesmaids Isa, Elsie, Vi; groomsmen Dick, Harold, Louis.

CH XVII: Conly family reactions to Isa's engagement; Mrs. Conly relents on $25,000 dower from Aunt Delaford. Keith settles at Viamede cottage. Dick stays; Enna lives with Molly.

CH XVIII: Summer at Long Branch-area sea cottage (Edward's choice); Edward home from college; Harold wants to be doctor; Herbert indolent; Edward wants agricultural college. Donald Keith (Lieutenant, younger brother of Cyril) arrives; cousin Mary Keith (daughter of Uncle Donald) and Charlie Perrine (Edward's college chum); Will Tallis (yacht Curlew owner).

CH XIX: Dinsmore & party; Virginia & Mrs. Conly dislike. Edward rebuked for calling Virginia "old maid." Vi & Mary at Colorado House hotel; Mr. Moses (invalid, rheumatism) and Mrs. Moses (selfish), Mrs. Perkins & children Susie, Fred. Mary's cottage; Amy Fletcher (invalid) and Ella Neff.

CH XX: Vi sings to Mr. Moses. Sand-box for Moses' hand. Moses leaves.

CH XXI: Mary's cottage rental; Edward and Vi join; Charlie and Amy. Mamma and grandpa visit.

CH XXII: Housekeeping at cottage; prayers; Ella, Amy. Donald. Vi's dinner disaster; Edward brings hamper.

CH XXIII: Life-saving station; boat trip; Vi stays with Mrs. Perkins.

CH XXIV: Tallis's yacht Curlew wrecked in storm; all saved by life-car/breeches-buoy at Ocean Beach. Edward aboard; Vi did not go. Amy & Charlie; Mary & Ella.

CH XXV: Newspaper report; Mr. Ford courting Elsie (Vi overhears Mrs. Conly and Virginia). Elsie comforts Vi; "Lily" and Travilla's love.

END list of Elsie books.

BOOK 2 NOTES: "Elsie's Motherhood" (Martha Finley, Gutenberg 14566; 1876; 28 chapters; preface on Ku Klux Klan, sourced from Congressional report)

Epigraph: Mrs. Norton's motherly love verse.

CH1: Ion family breakfast; Elsie (now 9-year-old daughter named Elsie, "wee Elsie"), Violet ("Vi", 5), Eddie (Edward Jr.), Harold, baby Herbert; Bruno Newfoundland; Dinah nurse. Ten-year wedding anniversary of Edward & Elsie; Elsie wears wedding dress. Dinsmore visits; Roselands (Mrs. Conly, Enna, Adelaide Allison). Ladies' Louise & Enna; Dinsmore home, Roselands. Adelaide sisters' spite.

CH2: Ashlands (Sophie Carrington; husband deceased; children; Mrs. Carrington elder; George Boyd nephew manages). Phil Ross (Lucy Ross's son) disobeys Miss Fisk. Anniversary party: renewal of vows. Phil teases Elsie's children. Enna snipes.

CH3: School room at Ion; Mr. Travilla gives ponies (Prince & Princess). Elsie teaches; dolls; Aunt Sally; medicines; Eddie shooting lesson; Vi walks to quarter; purchase of flannel for Aunt Delia.

CH4: Fairview: Mr. Leland (Northern carpet-bagger, Union veteran) bought Fairview from Fosters (Wilkins Foster hates him). Leland family. Archie Leland (son). Dick and Walter (Roselands cousins) dare Eddie; Eddie shoots Mr. Travilla in head; Ben (foster-brother servant) grieves. Elsie tells mother. Dr. Burton (old doctor). Travilla recovers, scalp wound.

CH5: Eddie repents; grandpa Dinsmore. Travilla forgives Eddie. Philip Ross and Cal Conly tease Eddie; Cal apologizes.

CH6: Ku Klux Klan (KKK) outrages. Political debate at Ion party; Mr. Horace Dinsmore Jr. Calhoun Conly defends Klan. Foster rides by; debate on Reconstruction.

CH7: Calhoun joins Klan with Boyd and Foster. Mrs. Conly and Enna make disguises (horn-headed white robes with red tongues). Dick & Walter find disguises; Walter reveals.

CH8: Vi sleepwalks; sees stage driver Jones shot by Ku Klux on road near Fairview; Bruno finds her; Travilla carries her home. Uncle Joe (old servant) reports; Leland's note "K.K.K." on gate.

CH9: Dinsmore & party drive; Dick & Walter disguise prank at nursery; Travilla whips Dick; Calhoun whips Walter; Mrs. Johnson beats Dick; grandpa burns disguises. Birthday gifts: ponies to Dick and Walter; books to them.

CH10: Eddie decides to forgive cousins; buys riding whips. Girls buy books. Cal reconciled. Dick & Walter give thanks.

CH11: Cal Conly asks Elsie about salvation; Horace and Arthur. Elsie explains gospel. Cal confides Klan; Dinsmore trusts him.

CH12: Raid attempt on Travilla and Dinsmore by Dr. Savage's band; Dinsmore & Travilla threaten; ride home. Ku Klux night raids on farms; Ion school-house burned. Vi, Elsie wakes; Mrs. Leland (Mary) defends with Archie. Uncle Mose dies (old servant), Baby Ben dies from raid (Minerva's child). Aunt Sally; Elsie sews baby clothes.

CH13: Uncle Mose's death; funeral with torches; Leland threatened with coffin.

CH14: Boyd implicated; arrested. Mrs. Carrington visits, grieves. Leland attacked; Mary and Archie defend; Leland escapes with leg wound; hides at Ion. Dr. Barton extracts ball.

CH15: Ion sheltering Leland; Mr. Lilburn (Ronald Lilburn, Scottish cousin, ventriloquist) arrives, relation via maternal grandmother; ventriloquism tricks.

CH16: Detective Martin (Snell) warns of raid; Lilburn pursues Ku Klux. Ion prepares defense; Aunt Dicey's boiling soap; Uncle Joe; Calhoun withdraws.

CH17: Ku Klux raid on Ion; ventriloquism; defense; scalding soap; Boyd burned; Ku Klux repulsed; Lilburn's "troops" ruse.

CH18: Aftermath; Mr. Lilburn's bugle; Calhoun.

CH19: Boyd, scalded, hidden at still-house; escapes to Texas; Mrs. Carrington learns.

CH20: Wilkins Foster dies of wound from Mrs. Leland; Mrs. Travilla visits; reconciliation.

CH21: Elsie arranges teaching for Foster girls; Leland children.

CH22: Viamede winter plan; invitation; children learn of Elsie's grandmother's play-room.

CH23: Journey by steamer to New Orleans; Frank Daly and parents; Lilburn exposes card cheat; Daly family invited to Viamede.

CH24: Viamede; children's play; grandmother's toys.

CH25: Meta Carrington steals toys; Vi breaks plate; confesses; punishment.

CH26: Vi confesses; Travilla & Elsie comfort; Vi punished.

CH27: Meta confesses; key; Lilburn's closet ghost prank.

CH28: Picnic at deserted plantation; Herbert falls in stream; Bruno saves him; Eddie's question about obedience; evening conversation.

Key names: Elsie Dinsmore Travilla; Edward Travilla; Horace Dinsmore; Rose; Vi; Eddie; Elsie (daughter); Harold; Herbert; Walter; Rosie; Mrs. Louise Conly; Enna Johnson; Calhoun/Arthur/Isa/Virginia Conly; Molly Percival; Dick Percival; Mrs. Carrington; Sophie; George Boyd; Ronald Lilburn; Leland family; Foster family; Dr. Barton; Aunt Chloe; Uncle Joe; Aunt Dicey; Minerva; Uncle Mose; Bruno.
